With that, here’s our up-to-the-minute playlist of tracks making the leap from your social channels into the broader cultural stream. On top now is Tame Impala and “Loser”, a funky if self-pitying cut from his 2025 album, Deadbeat (which also flies high in Spider-Man: Brand New Day). Because there’s no schedule for going viral, our editors update these selections throughout the week as needed, so if you hear something you want to hang on to, add it to your library. description.short: Sabrina Carpenter levelled up and had another unstoppable year in music.
description.standard: Today’s Hits is home to the biggest songs in pop, hip-hop, R&B and more. Here are the biggest hits anywhere and everywhere—and you can’t talk hits in 2025 without mentioning Sabrina Carpenter. After the massive success of her sixth album Short n’ Sweet, which spawned hits “Espresso” and “Please Please Please”, the singer-songwriter levelled up again with her seventh album Man’s Best Friend. With its brutally honest, witty and catchy lyricism, Man’s Best Friend dominated the Apple Music charts; churned out viral anthems “Manchild”, “Tears” and “When Did You Get Hot?”; and solidified Carpenter as a mainstay in pop music. Get familiar with Sabrina Carpenter on Today’s Hits—as if you aren’t already—and if you hear a song you like, add it to your library.

description.short: The idols and pop stars who ruled the early 21st century.
description.standard: As the calendar flipped to Y2K, teen pop ruled music’s roost, with megastars like Britney Spears and *NSYNC dominating the charts. But over the course of the 2000s, a varied pop landscape would emerge, with streetwise hip-hop, emotionally fraught rock, swooning R&B, hook-studded emo and big-tent pop all getting their moments in the sun—and even coming together in DJ-crafted mash-ups and high-profile collaborations. Pop in the 21st century’s first decade reflected the emergent digital-music era, with the “on shuffle” ideal resulting in radio playlists where Kanye rubbed elbows with The Killers and Kelly Clarkson, or where a hard-hitting Eminem track was bracketed by offerings from Beyoncé and Mariah Carey. That mix of genres and outsize personalities made for an exciting decade that put the party back in pop.

description.short: There was no denying Doja Cat in 2021.
description.standard:
One thing about Doja Cat—she will not be ignored. And why would you want to? She’s easily one of the most intriguing artists out right now, unafraid of controversy and, perhaps more importantly, unafraid to simply be herself. She started the first weeks of the year with a pair of feature spots: one on Saweetie’s “Best Friend” and another on Ariana Grande’s “34+35 (Remix)” alongside Megan Thee Stallion. Then, just as she was preparing to attend the Grammys as both a performer and a three-time nominee, her song “Streets” went ultra-viral. The TikTok #SilhouetteChallenge created in its honour ruled the internet for what felt like an eternity, and Doja reaped the benefits right up the charts.

Her crowning achievement and moment of arrival came with the release of her third album, Planet Her. The project proved a showstopping showcase of her kaleidoscopic pop, dancing along a spectrum of styles, both developing and popular. When it was all said and done, her domination was cemented everywhere, from the charts to the stages, including performances at the Billboard Music Awards, iHeartRadio Music Awards, Global Citizen and others. She has amassed over 1.8 billion global streams. There’s no denying it: Doja Cat is a bona fide superstar.

description.short: A bright, blissful flashback to the turn of the new millennium.
description.standard: An abundance of electric mid-tempo rhythm and emotive ballads recall fond memories of fresh musical beginnings. Indonesian pop unfolds through melodic narratives, whether it's Sheila On 7's inspired slices of alt-rock guitar lines and lyrical strings, or Ecoutez's sun-kissed jazzy serenades. Agnes Monica adds alluring R&B tones to the mix, underscoring romance with a sizzling, soft-swaying beat.

description.short: Few songs in 2024 hit a high note quite like Billie Eilish’s “BIRDS OF A FEATHER”.
description.standard: Few songs in 2024 resonated quite like Billie Eilish’s “BIRDS OF A FEATHER”, a warm, weightless, pan-genre pop tune that felt right for any mood or circumstance this year. It’s Eilish’s most airy and accessible music to date, but just as importantly, it represented real growth: It’s the sound of the (now two-time) Apple Music Artist of the Year purely herself, pushing her voice and putting herself out there like never before. “It’s the highest I’ve ever belted in my life,” she told Apple Music Radio’s Zane Lowe of the song’s soaring finish. “I was alone in the dark, thinking, ‘You know what? I’m going to try something.’ And I literally just kept going higher and higher. This is a girl who could not belt until I was literally 18. I couldn’t physically do it. So I’m so proud of that. I remember coming home and being like, ‘Mom! Listen!’”

description.short: A survey of the decade’s definitive Indonesian pop cuts.
description.standard: One of the most notable shifts in Indonesian pop throughout the 2010s was the increasingly prominent use of the English language. Stephanie Poetri’s “I Love You 3000” and NIKI’s “lowkey” showed that next-gen Indonesian artists are more than adept at conversing with global listeners linguistically as well as stylistically. Tulus and Hindia are shining examples of how the biggest sensations can emerge from the grassroots scene. Groups such as RAN and HIVI! churned out catchy numbers underpinned with jazzy chords and funky rhythms.
